profile.reading:
NocRoom is a regionally focused internet infrastructure and IT services company operating out of South Florida, describing on its own website a footprint spanning Miami, Los Angeles, Dallas, Las Vegas, and Fremont, California. In those markets the company advertises colocation, IP transit, and other network-based services, VPS hosting on SSD storage in RAID 10+1 configurations, and dedicated IPv4 and IPv6 addressing. Around Miami specifically, NocRoom also markets local IT integration work distinct from colocation: installing fiber and copper network runs, self-hosted PBX and VoIP telephony, email systems, IP routing, and server or virtualization support, so the company functions as much as a regional IT services provider as a pure data-center operator.

This entry is one of two points OpenStreetMap contributors have separately mapped under the name "NocRoom Miami IT Services" in the greater Miami area, roughly twenty kilometers apart, and the available public record does not establish whether the two points describe genuinely separate facilities, a single business location mapped twice, or one accurate point alongside a duplicate. NocRoom's own site describes its presence at the level of the metropolitan market rather than by street address, and no government record, permit filing, or news account tying a confirmed facility to this exact location was found. The nearest addressable building to this entry's recorded coordinates sits along Northwest 19th Street near Miami International Airport, in a corridor of light-industrial and logistics buildings that is a more plausible setting for network or colocation infrastructure than a typical office park, though that plausibility is circumstantial rather than confirmed - nothing in NocRoom's own materials names this address as a company facility.

This entry should be read as documenting NocRoom's general presence in the Miami market rather than as a verified profile of a specific building. NocRoom appears to be a real, operating South Florida internet and IT services business - what is not established here is which, if any, of the addresses associated with its name in public mapping data corresponds to an actual data center or network facility it operates, and readers should treat both mapped Miami points with that caveat in mind. Anyone needing a verified street address for NocRoom's Miami operations should contact the company directly rather than rely on either coordinate pair recorded in this registry.

reading.body:
This facility's published specifications contain no power capacity, no IT load, no cooling capacity, and no statement of buildout status. Without these figures, the campus cannot be assessed for relevance to AI scaling.

NocRoom describes itself as a colocation and IT services provider across three cities. The specific facility mapped here ranks fifth among Florida's facilities with published power capacity, though it has contributed none of its own to that ranking. Florida has published capacity of 9.35 MW across four facilities that disclose figures, making the state a minor player in data center capacity. This campus's position in the state cannot be determined from operator disclosures.

The operator's own site does not confirm a street address for this facility. Reverse geocoding places the coordinates near Miami International Airport, while an aggregator lists a separate NocRoom facility downtown, 12 kilometers away. Without operator confirmation of which location this row describes, or of any power and IT specifications, no reading of this campus's role in AI infrastructure is possible from published sources.
